# FM-SWITCH

> An app for iPhone, iPad and Mac for swapping M-VAVE FM-1 firmwares over USB. In TestFlight for iPhone and iPad, a download for the Mac, open source, free, not affiliated with M-VAVE.

Part of Drew Robinson's FM-1 projects: https://fm-1.drewr.dev/ (see /llms-full.txt there for the others). Source: https://github.com/ocean/FM-SWITCH

## What it's for

The M-VAVE FM-1 is a tiny hardware synthesiser with a lively community of custom firmwares (Felucca, GHOULBOX, ESTAMPIE, X0X, Melodee and more). Installing them has usually meant a computer and a Chrome-based web installer. FM-SWITCH lets someone plug their FM-1 into an iPhone, iPad or Mac, pick a firmware and install it, and switch back whenever they like.

## Features

- Firmware list: the firmware hub's catalogue (thefirmwarehub.com), fm1-editor.com's list, aroum's FM1 Resource Hub and mutant.cloud, sorted by name, latest update or most installed (The Firmware Hub's install counts), with filters for kinds (grooveboxes, synths and so on) and for firmwares built from source. The app remembers the sort and filter, and keeps them at the top of the list while scrolling.
- Firmware pages: each firmware's own page, with its author, description, pictures from its README, an Install button, Save to this phone for later, and its links (project site, source code, release, editor, try it in the browser, and the lists it's on).
- Package discovery: finds each firmware's `.fwsc` package from GitHub releases, publisher manifests, project pages or M-VAVE's downloads, with live checks for newer releases and their builds.
- Saved firmwares: kept on the device for offline flashing, in My firmwares, which has its own sort and filters. Saving a new release of a firmware keeps the ones saved before, so an older release can be installed again.
- M-VAVE's official V15 comes with the app, unmodified (from M-VAVE's open-source fm1_open, Apache-2.0), so there's always a known-good firmware to go back to.
- Flashing, through FM1Kit: checks the package before anything is sent; with more than one FM-1 connected, asks which one to use; asks before switching to a different firmware (which can erase the FM-1's projects and samples); refuses V15 over V15; pauses auto-lock and asks iOS for background time during a flash; if it stops for any reason, the person is told not to switch the FM-1 off, to plug it back in and carry on where it left off; the install is done as soon as the FM-1 starts the new firmware, and if it takes a while to come back, FM-SWITCH looks for it again before calling the install failed.
- Switching between firmwares (from 0.2.0): before installing, FM-SWITCH says what switching back from that firmware will take, using FM1Kit's leaving guides. When the firmware on the FM-1 won't take the one picked (AMB-1, DUB-1 or HYP-1 back to V15, V16 or Open, for example), it puts MIDIMON on first, then the one picked, and says why. It warns before installing V16 (going back to V15 needs a Mac) and before installing V15 after V16 (V15 plays one note at a time until its saved data is cleared). FM-1s with the newer flash chip get a warning before a firmware that only knows the older one.
- Installing shows one progress bar through three stages: getting ready, installing and restarting. The FM-1's screen stays dark while it installs.
- Each install's log is saved in ~/Library/Logs/FM-SWITCH on the Mac, to send if something goes wrong.
- Save my FM-1: on M-VAVE's open firmware, keeps a copy of every saved project, the project being edited (with unsaved changes) and the samples, before switching away.
- An install takes about 20 seconds for V15 and under 40 seconds for Felucca 1.6.1 on the FM-1 tested.
- Whole-flash backups (Mac): with the FM-1 in download mode, backs up its whole flash and restores it later. Before every backup or restore, macOS asks for the person's password so FM-SWITCH's helper can run as an administrator, then for permission to use the FM-1 as a USB drive. Hardware-tested with the notarised build on 29 Oct 2026. Backup & rescue also gets V16 from M-VAVE (checked by its hash) and installs it with its own bootloader, can start the new firmware fresh by clearing the old one's saved data, and installs m-bootloader 2.1 (MIT), which also starts on an FM-1 that has had V16; m-bootloader hasn't yet been tried on the newer flash chip.
- Flash history, and a simulated FM-1 for the iOS Simulator (it can start in USB rescue mode, or "pull the cable" at 45% to test carrying on).

## Platforms

- iOS and iPadOS 17 or later (sandboxed, as every App Store and TestFlight app is), and macOS 14 or later; native SwiftUI on both.
- The Mac app is signed with Developer ID and notarised by Apple. It isn't sandboxed: reading or writing the FM-1's whole flash runs a small tool as an administrator, and macOS asks for your password first.
- Connects by an iPhone or iPad's USB-C port, a Lightning device through Apple's camera adapter, or a Mac's USB.
- iPad (landscape, or a 13-inch in either orientation) and the Mac get a wide layout: a sidebar, and lists with the picked item beside them.

## Look

Standard, the app's everyday look: a warm parchment ground (#EEE8DD; #141413 in dark mode), white cards, the system font, purple for firmware (#6D28D9), orange for buttons and switches (#C2410C), and a drawn FM-1 on the home screen that shows each install's progress. Light, dark or following the device. The app icon is that FM-1 on purple, with swap arrows on its screen.

Retro, hidden until found and then chosen in Settings: the original 8-bit handheld-console screen, near-black (#0C0E0D) with a green accent (#7BE39A), Silkscreen pixel capitals, Departure Mono and VT323, notched pixel boxes and a segmented progress bar. It has its own app icon.

The website's FM-SWITCH page has both looks: https://fm-1.drewr.dev/fm-switch/ and https://fm-1.drewr.dev/fm-switch/retro/

## Tips

Every feature is free, and tips unlock nothing. On iPhone and iPad tips are in-app purchases; on the Mac, Ko-fi (https://ko-fi.com/oceanicity).

## Building

iPhone and iPad: in TestFlight now; ask on the FM-1 Discord for more. Mac: a signed, notarised DMG from the website, always at https://github.com/ocean/FM-SWITCH/releases/latest/download/FM-SWITCH.dmg

The Mac app checks GitHub once a day for a newer release; the request carries nothing about the person or their FM-1.

## Under the hood

Talking to the FM-1 (the update protocol, `.fwsc` packages, CoreMIDI and the simulated FM-1) is FM1Kit, an open-source Swift package by the same author: https://fm-1.drewr.dev/fm1kit/ (source: https://github.com/ocean/FM1Kit)

## Safety

Not affiliated with M-VAVE. Installing custom firmware is at the owner's own risk.
